newsitem.title: USA: Chicago plan panel backs two developments - papers.
newsitem.headline: Chicago plan panel backs two developments - papers.

text.p: Chicago Plan Commission has advanced a proposed $60 million hotel development near downtown and a $45 million movie theater and retail sales complex on the city's northern border, Chicago newspapers reported Friday.
Dallas-based Wyndham Hotels & Resorts would own the hotel to be developed from an office building by Oxford Capital Partners, Chicago Sun-Times reported.
Construction on the 418-room Wyndham hotel would begin in January for completion by fall 1998, the Sun-Times said.

The retail and movie theater complex on the border between Chicago and Evanston would be developed by DevCorp North and the Combined Property Development Corp and includes $8 million of city backing from a tax increment financing district, Chicago Tribune said.
Cineplex Odeon and Dominick's Finer Foods would be included in the development, the Tribune said.
Both projects must be approved by the Chicago City Council.
